accepted.question_text: Given the adjacency matrix of a graph G, determine whether there exists a finite set P of points in the plane whose visibility graph is exactly G, where two points of P are adjacent exactly when the segment joining them contains or passes through no other point of P.

evidence.quote: We say two points pi and pj of P are mutually visible if the line segment pi pj does not contain or pass through any other point of P.

The visibility graph (also called the point visibility graph) G of P is defined by associating a vertex vi with each point pi of P such that (vi , vj ) is an undirected edge of G if pi and pj are mutually visible.
Open Problem 1 Given a graph G in adjacency matrix form, determine whether G is the visibility graph of a set of points P in the plane.

accepted.question_text: Characterize exactly which graphs arise as visibility graphs of finite point sets in the plane, where two points are adjacent when the segment joining them contains or passes through no other point of the set.

evidence.quote: We say two points pi and pj of P are mutually visible if the line segment pi pj does not contain or pass through any other point of P.

The visibility graph (also called the point visibility graph) G of P is defined by associating a vertex vi with each point pi of P such that (vi , vj ) is an undirected edge of G if pi and pj are mutually visible.
Open Problem 2 Characterize visibility graphs of point sets.

accepted.question_text: Given a graph G known to be the visibility graph of a finite point set P in the plane, construct coordinates for a point set whose visibility graph is G.

evidence.quote: We say two points pi and pj of P are mutually visible if the line segment pi pj does not contain or pass through any other point of P.

The visibility graph (also called the point visibility graph) G of P is defined by associating a vertex vi with each point pi of P such that (vi , vj ) is an undirected edge of G if pi and pj are mutually visible.
Open Problem 3 Given the visibility graph G of a set of points, draw the points in the plane whose visibility graph is G.

accepted.question_text: Prove that every visibility graph of a point set with clique number omega(G) <= 4 has chromatic number chi(G) <= 5.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1 There exists a function f such that chi(G) <= f (omega(G)).
Open Problem 4 Prove that every visibility graph with omega(G) <= 4 has chi(G) <= 5.

accepted.question_text: Prove that there is a constant c such that every visibility graph of a point set with clique number omega(G) = 5 satisfies chi(G) <= c.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1 There exists a function f such that chi(G) <= f (omega(G)).
Open Problem 5 Prove Conjecture 1 for visibility graphs with omega(G) = 5.

accepted.question_text: For integers k >= 2 and ell >= 2, every sufficiently large planar point set should contain either ell collinear points or k mutually visible points. Prove this in the remaining open cases k = 6 or ell = 4.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2 For all integers k >= 2 and ell >= 2, there is an integer h(k, ell) such that any point set P of at least h(k, ell) points in the plane contains ell collinear points, or k mutually visible points.
Open Problem 6 Prove Conjecture 2 for k = 6 or ell = 4.

accepted.question_text: Let b(P) be the minimum size of a blocking set Q for a finite point set P in general position, and let b(n) be the minimum of b(P) over all n-point sets with no three points collinear. Prove that b(n)/n tends to infinity as n tends to infinity.

evidence.quote: Any such set Q is called a blocking set for P.
Let b(P ) denote the smallest size blocking set Q for P . Let b(n) denote the minimum of b(P ) for all P having n points with no three points being collinear.
Open Problem 7 Prove that as n -> infinity, b(n) / n -> infinity.

accepted.question_text: Is every n-vertex graph representable by an obstacle representation that uses only O(n) polygonal obstacles, where vertices are points in the plane and two vertices are adjacent exactly when the segment joining the corresponding points avoids every obstacle?

evidence.quote: We call the pair (P, Q) as obstacle representation of G.
The obstacle number of G is the minimum number of obstacles required in any obstacle representation of G.
Open Problem 8 Is the obstacle number of a graph with n vertices bounded above by a linear function of n?

accepted.question_text: Improve the current lower bound O(n / log^2 n) for the maximum possible obstacle number of an n-vertex graph.

evidence.quote: We call the pair (P, Q) as obstacle representation of G.
The obstacle number of G is the minimum number of obstacles required in any obstacle representation of G.
Open Problem 9 Improve the present lower bound O(n/ log2 n) of the obstacle number of a graph with n vertices.

accepted.question_text: For each integer h > 1, determine the smallest number of vertices that a graph can have while having obstacle number exactly h.

evidence.quote: We call the pair (P, Q) as obstacle representation of G.
The obstacle number of G is the minimum number of obstacles required in any obstacle representation of G.
Open Problem 10 For h > 1, what is the smallest number of vertices of a graph with obstacle number h?

accepted.question_text: Does every planar graph have obstacle number 1?

evidence.quote: We call the pair (P, Q) as obstacle representation of G.
The obstacle number of G is the minimum number of obstacles required in any obstacle representation of G.
Open Problem 11 Does every planar graph have obstacle number 1?

accepted.question_text: Given the adjacency matrix of a graph G, determine whether there exists a set S of pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane whose segment visibility graph is G, where vertices correspond to segment endpoints and two endpoints are adjacent when the segment joining them avoids all segments of S, with the two endpoints of each original segment also adjacent.

evidence.quote: We say two points pi and pj of P are mutually visible if the line segment pi pj does not intersect any segment si in S.

The visibility graph (also called the segment visibility graph or segment endpoint visibility graph) G of S is defined by associating a vertex vi with each point pi of P such that (vi , vj ) is an undirected edge of G if pi and pj are mutually visible.
In addition, the corresponding vertices of two endpoints of every segment in S is also connected by an edge in G.
Open Problem 12 Given a graph G in adjacency matrix form, determine whether G is the segment visibility graph of a set of disjoint segments S in the plane.

accepted.question_text: Characterize exactly which graphs arise as segment visibility graphs of finite collections of pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane.

evidence.quote: We say two points pi and pj of P are mutually visible if the line segment pi pj does not intersect any segment si in S.

The visibility graph (also called the segment visibility graph or segment endpoint visibility graph) G of S is defined by associating a vertex vi with each point pi of P such that (vi , vj ) is an undirected edge of G if pi and pj are mutually visible.
Open Problem 13 Characterize the segment visibility graphs.

accepted.question_text: Given a graph G known to be a segment visibility graph, construct a set of pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane whose segment visibility graph is G.

evidence.quote: We say two points pi and pj of P are mutually visible if the line segment pi pj does not intersect any segment si in S.

The visibility graph (also called the segment visibility graph or segment endpoint visibility graph) G of S is defined by associating a vertex vi with each point pi of P such that (vi , vj ) is an undirected edge of G if pi and pj are mutually visible.
Open Problem 14 Given a segment visibility graph G, draw the segments S in the plane whose visibility graph is G.

accepted.question_text: Given the adjacency matrix of a segment visibility graph G, find a Hamiltonian cycle of G in polynomial time.
accepted.context_brief: Hamiltonian cycles in segment visibility graphs

evidence.quote: Consider the problem of identifying a Hamiltonian cycle C in G.
Open Problem 15 Given a segment visibility graph G in adjacency matrix form, identify a Hamiltonian cycle in G in polynomial time.

accepted.question_text: Given the adjacency matrix of a segment visibility graph G, identify which edges of G correspond to the original segments of the underlying segment set S.

evidence.quote: In addition, the corresponding vertices of two endpoints of every segment in S is also connected by an edge in G.
Open Problem 16 Given a segment visibility graph G in adjacency matrix form, identify the edges of G that correspond to segments of S.

accepted.question_text: Characterize exactly which graphs admit a unit bar visibility representation, meaning a bar visibility representation in which all horizontal bars have the same length.

evidence.quote: Suppose, a restriction is imposed that all bars in a visibility representation must have the same length. In that case, we get another type of visibility graphs which are known as unit bar visibility graphs.
Open Problem 17 Characterize unit bar visibility graphs.

accepted.question_text: Is recognizing unit bar visibility graphs an NP-complete problem?

evidence.quote: Suppose, a restriction is imposed that all bars in a visibility representation must have the same length. In that case, we get another type of visibility graphs which are known as unit bar visibility graphs.
Open Problem 18 Is recognition of unit bar visibility graphs NP-complete?

accepted.question_text: Characterize exactly which graphs are bar k-visibility graphs, where vertices are horizontal bars and two bars are adjacent exactly when some vertical segment between them intersects at most k other bars.

evidence.quote: Formally, a graph G is called a bar k-visibility graph if its vertices v1 , v2 , . . . , vn can be associated with a set S of disjoint line segments (or, horizontal bars) s1 , s2 , . . . , sn in the plane such that vi and vj are joined by an edge in G if and only if a vertical segment between si and sj intersects at most k segments of S.
Open Problem 19 Characterize bar k-visibility graphs.

accepted.question_text: Triangle-free non-planar graphs are already known to be forbidden subgraphs of bar k-visibility graphs. Determine whether there are other classes of forbidden subgraphs for bar k-visibility graphs.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 20 Triangle-free non-planar graphs are forbidden subgraphs of bar k-visibility graphs. Is there any other class of forbidden subgraphs of bar k-visibility graphs?

accepted.question_text: For k >= 5, determine whether there exist (2k + 2)-regular bar k-visibility graphs.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 21 Are there (2k + 2)-regular bar k-visibility graphs for k >= 5?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether there exist d-regular bar k-visibility graphs with degree d >= 2k + 3.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 22 Are there d-regular bar k-visibility graphs with d >= 2k + 3?

accepted.question_text: Improve the current upper bound 6k + 6 on the chromatic number of a bar k-visibility graph.
accepted.context_brief: Chromatic number of bar k-visibility graphs

evidence.quote: Dean et al. [24] also proved that 6k + 6 is an upper bound on the chromatic number of G.
Open Problem 23 Improve the current upper bound of 6k + 6 on the chromatic number of a bar k-visibility graph.

accepted.question_text: The thickness of a bar k-visibility graph is known to be at most 2k(9k - 1). Improve this upper bound.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 24 It has been shown that the thickness of a bar k-visibility graph is bounded by 2k(9k - 1). Can this upper bound be improved?

accepted.question_text: What is the largest possible crossing number of a bar k-visibility graph?
accepted.context_brief: Crossing numbers of bar k-visibility graphs

evidence.quote: Open Problem 25 The crossing number of a graph is the minimum possible number of crossings with which the graph can be drawn in the plane. What is the largest crossing number of a bar k-visibility graph?

accepted.question_text: What is the largest possible genus of a bar k-visibility graph?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 26 The genus of a graph is the minimal integer g such that the graph can be embedded on a surface of genus g. What is the largest genus of a bar k-visibility graph?

accepted.question_text: Characterize exactly which graphs are rectangle visibility graphs, where vertices are isothetic rectangles with pairwise disjoint interiors and two vertices are adjacent exactly when their rectangles are horizontally or vertically visible by an unobstructed beam of finite width.

evidence.quote: A graph G is called a rectangle visibility graph if it can be realized by closed isothetic rectangles in the plane, with pairwise disjoint interiors, with vertices representing rectangles in such a way that two vertices vi and vj of G are connected by an edge if and only if their corresponding rectangles are vertically or horizontally visible from each other by a beam of unobstructed visibility of finite width.
Open Problem 27 Characterize rectangle visibility graphs.

accepted.question_text: Given the adjacency matrix of a graph G, determine whether there exists a simple polygon P whose vertex visibility graph is G, where two vertices of P are adjacent exactly when the segment joining them lies entirely inside P.

evidence.quote: We say two points a and b in P are mutually visible if the line segment ab lies entirely within P.

The visibility graph (also called the vertex visibility graph) G of P is defined by associating a node with each vertex of P such that (vi , vj ) is an undirected edge of G if polygonal vertices vi and vj are mutually visible.
Open Problem 28 Given a graph G in adjacency matrix form, determine whether G is the visibility graph of a simple polygon P .

accepted.question_text: Is the problem of recognizing whether a graph is the visibility graph of a simple polygon in NP?

evidence.quote: The general problem of recognizing a given graph G as the visibility graph of a simple polygon P is yet to be solved.
Open Problem 29 Is the problem of recognizing visibility graphs in NP ?

accepted.question_text: Given the adjacency matrix of a graph G together with a Hamiltonian cycle C of G, determine whether G is the visibility graph of a simple polygon P whose boundary order is exactly the cycle C.

evidence.quote: Ghosh [53, 55] presented three necessary conditions for recognizing visibility graphs G of a simple polygon P under the assumption that a Hamiltonian cycle C of G, which corresponds to the boundary of P , is given as input along with G.

Open Problem 30 Given a graph G in adjacency matrix form along with a Hamiltonian cycle C of G, determine whether G is the visibility graph of a simple polygon P whose boundary corresponds to the given Hamiltonian cycle C.

accepted.question_text: Characterize exactly which graphs arise as visibility graphs of simple polygons.

evidence.quote: We say two points a and b in P are mutually visible if the line segment ab lies entirely within P.

The visibility graph (also called the vertex visibility graph) G of P is defined by associating a node with each vertex of P such that (vi , vj ) is an undirected edge of G if polygonal vertices vi and vj are mutually visible.
Open Problem 32 Characterize visibility graphs of simple polygons.

accepted.question_text: Given a graph G known to be the visibility graph of a simple polygon, construct a simple polygon whose visibility graph is G.

evidence.quote: The problem of actually drawing a simple polygon P whose visibility graph is the given graph G, is called the visibility graph reconstruction problem for polygons.
Open Problem 33 Draw a simple polygon whose visibility graph is the given graph G.

accepted.question_text: Given the visibility graph G of a simple polygon P, determine which Hamiltonian cycle of G corresponds to the boundary of P.

evidence.quote: Observe that G may contain several Hamiltonian cycles, and G may be visibility graph for a Hamiltonian cycle and is not a valid visibility graph for another Hamiltonian cycle in G.
Open Problem 34 Given the visibility graph G of a simple polygon P , determine the Hamiltonian cycle in G that corresponds to the boundary of P .

accepted.question_text: Design a constant-factor approximation algorithm for the minimum dominating set problem on visibility graphs of simple polygons.

evidence.quote: A dominating set for a graph G = (V, E) is a subset D of V such that every vertex not in D is joined to at least one member of D by some edge.
Open Problem 35 Design a constant factor approximation algorithm for computing minimum dominating set of visibility graphs.

accepted.question_text: Given the visibility graph G of a simple polygon P together with the Hamiltonian cycle of G corresponding to the boundary of P, determine a maximum hidden set of G, meaning a largest set of vertices no two of which are adjacent.
accepted.context_brief: Maximum hidden sets with boundary order

evidence.quote: An independent set is a set of vertices in a graph with no two of which are adjacent. Independent sets in visibility graphs are known as hidden vertex sets.
Open Problem 36 Given the visibility graph G of a simple polygon P along with the Hamiltonian cycle in G corresponding to the boundary of P , determine the maximum hidden set of G.

accepted.question_text: Design an approximation algorithm for computing a maximum hidden set in a visibility graph.

evidence.quote: Independent sets in visibility graphs are known as hidden vertex sets.
Open Problem 37 Design an approximation algorithm for computing maximum hidden set of visibility graph.

accepted.question_text: Given the adjacency matrix of a visibility graph G, compute a maximum clique of G.

evidence.quote: A clique in a graph is a set of pairwise adjacent vertices.
Open Problem 38 Given a visibility graph G in adjacency matrix form, compute a maximum clique of G.

accepted.question_text: Improve the current lower and upper bounds on the number of non-isomorphic visibility graphs of simple polygons with n vertices.

evidence.quote: It has been shown by Ghosh [55] that the number of non-isomorphic visibility graphs of simple polygons of n vertices is at least 2^(n-4).
On the other hand, a straightforward application of Warren's theorem [116] shows that the number of visibility graphs is at most 2^(O(n log n)) [106].
Open Problem 40 Improve the lower and upper bounds on the number of non-isomorphic visibility graphs of simple polygons.

accepted.question_text: Can every visibility graph be realized so that all endpoint coordinates are integers using only polynomially many bits per coordinate?

evidence.quote: However, it is not known whether singly exponential sized integers are sufficient.
It is important because if we could guarantee that the number of bits in the integer is polynomial, then visibility graph recognition is in NP [106].
Open Problem 41 Can all endpoints of a visibility graph be assigned integer coordinates such that the integers use a polynomial number of bits?

accepted.question_text: Determine the correct asymptotic order of the minimum number of bits needed by an optimal covering-set representation of a visibility graph, where a covering set is a family of cliques and complete bipartite graphs whose members are subgraphs of the visibility graph and whose union covers every edge.

evidence.quote: The authors consider the problem of representing a visibility graph as a covering set of cliques and complete bipartite graphs so that every graph in the set is a subset of G, and every edge is contained in at least one of the graphs of the covering set.
Their proposed algorithm constructs a covering set which has O(n log4 n) bits. It can be shown that any covering set requires Omega(n log2 n) bits on some visibility graphs [106].
Open Problem 42 Give a tight bound (with respect to order notation) on the number of bits used in an optimal covering set of a visibility graph.

accepted.question_text: Find a polynomial-time algorithm that constructs a covering set for a visibility graph matching the optimal asymptotic bit bound.

evidence.quote: The authors consider the problem of representing a visibility graph as a covering set of cliques and complete bipartite graphs so that every graph in the set is a subset of G, and every edge is contained in at least one of the graphs of the covering set.
Open Problem 43 Find a covering set which matches the above bound in polynomial time.

accepted.question_text: For each integer k, does there exist an integer n such that every k-blocked point set has at most n points? Here a k-blocked point set is a set of planar points colored with k colors so that mutually visible points receive different colors and points that are not visible because of collinear blockers receive the same color.
accepted.context_brief: Bounded size of k-blocked point sets

evidence.quote: The problem is to assign k >= 2 colours to points of P such that (i) if two points are mutually visible in P , assign different colours to them, and (ii) if two points are not visible due to some collinear points in P , assign the same colour to both of them.
Any set of points that admits such a colouring with k colours (for a fixed k) is called a k-blocked point set.
Conjecture 3 For each integer k, there is an integer n such that every k-blocked point set has at most n points.

accepted.question_text: Does every k-blocked point set have O(k^2) points?
accepted.context_brief: Quadratic bound for k-blocked point sets

evidence.quote: The problem is to assign k >= 2 colours to points of P such that (i) if two points are mutually visible in P , assign different colours to them, and (ii) if two points are not visible due to some collinear points in P , assign the same colour to both of them.
Any set of points that admits such a colouring with k colours (for a fixed k) is called a k-blocked point set.
Conjecture 4 Every k-blocked point set has O(k^2 ) points.

accepted.question_text: In every k-blocked point set, must each color class contain at most k points?
accepted.context_brief: Color-class size in k-blocked point sets

evidence.quote: The problem is to assign k >= 2 colours to points of P such that (i) if two points are mutually visible in P , assign different colours to them, and (ii) if two points are not visible due to some collinear points in P , assign the same colour to both of them.
Any set of points that admits such a colouring with k colours (for a fixed k) is called a k-blocked point set.
colour classes correspond to partition of points of P into independent sets.
Conjecture 5 In every k-blocked point set, there are at most k points in each colour class.

accepted.question_text: Does every visibility graph G with minimum degree delta(G) have vertex-connectivity at least (2 delta(G) + 1) / 3?

evidence.quote: Let kappa(H) and lambda(H) denote the vertex and edge connectivity of H respectively. Let delta(H) denote the minimum degree of H.
Conjecture 6 Every visibility graph G with minimum degree delta(G) has vertex-connectivity at least (2delta(G)+1)/3.

needs_review.question_text_raw: Open Problem 39 Determine whether a set of vertices of a visibility graph has a triangle-extendible ordering in polynomial time.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 39 Determine whether a set of vertices of a visibility graph has a triangle- extendible ordering in polynomial time.
Spinrad [106] has discussed possible approaches for computing maximum clique using the notion of triangle-extendible ordering which is essentially a transitive orientation of the graph.

needs_review.question_text_raw: Open Problem 31 Design an algorithm for testing Necessary Condition 4 in polynomial time.

evidence.quote: Necessary condition 4. Let D be any ordered cycle of the visibility graph G of a simple polygon P . For any assignment of blocking vertices to all minimal invisible pairs in G, the total number of vertices of D assigned to the minimal invisible pairs between the vertices of D is at most |D| - 3.
Open Problem 31 Design an algorithm for testing Necessary Condition 4 in polynomial time.
